articleTitle: The development of real-time software for multiple microprocessor-based systems: A case study
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A microprocessor-based system for the transfer of data between two different makes of minicomputer systems has been developed. Due to performance requirements, two processors were used. The high level language RTL/2 was used to develop the software for the system. A mechanism which allows efficient handling of interrupts and efficient signalling between interrupt handlers and user tasks is described. A method which allows simple allocation of duties between the processors, and which also allows performance tuning, is explained. Experience with the use of a development environment for RTL/2 (called MAGIC) and the use of a real-time executive (called SMT) is discussed. Finally, methods of synchronisation of the processors at start-up and resource sharing during regular processing are examined.

articleTitle: Optimization of physical parameters in linear turbogenerator controllers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The linear-quadratic optimal output feedback theory has been published often and is well known. However, the number of reports on various controller designs seems to lag far behind. In some applications, design engineers are reluctant to use LQ-theory because of the lack of a direct link to physical parameters of a controller. In this paper, the almost obvious link between arbitrary physical parameters and the commonly known minimization of the quadratic performance index is established and an application to the output feedback design for a turbo-generator controller is demonstrated on a turbogenerator susceptible to torsional oscillations. A model reduction technique is used to reduce the order of the system from 26 to 6 for the purpose of designing the controller.

articleTitle: Synchronization of frequency hopped spread spectrum signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The frequency hopped spread spectrum waveform is commonly used by mobile communications systems for its ability to combat interference, its inherent frequency diversity and its multiple access capability. It is therefore to be expected that these systems will be operated over channels subject to fading and interference. Since synchronization is a vital aspect of spread spectrum communications, it is important to predict synchronization performance in such adverse environments. A theoretical analysis of frequency hopped signal detection and synchronization strategies is presented. A typical system for the acquisition and tracking of frequency hopped signals is discussed and its performance characterised. This paper is tutorial in nature and collates and extends the work of [1] and [2].

articleTitle: Lighting and colour quality in a television system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper outlines a novel experiment that was conducted in an attempt to quantify the performance of different electric lamps from the point of view of television colour reproduction. The experiment examined the subjective responses of television viewers to changes in picture quality resulting from changes in the (studio) scene illumination. This led to the establishment of a Mean Subjective Rating (MSR) for each test source. Secondly, an attempt was made to correlate this subjective data with measured colour differences, in the television picture, resulting from the same changes in the studio lighting. Only moderate correlation was detected. Further investigation established, however, that there was significant correlation between the MSR and the CIE colour rendering index of each test source. The possibility of applying some of the newer varieties of light sources to television lighting is analysed, using these findings.

articleTitle: Provisions of anew high voltage research laboratory at conditions of reduced air density
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper outlines the rationale behind the construction of a modern outdoor high-voltage research laboratory at a high-altitude site in South Africa. One of the fundamental research objectives at this laboratory is to determine the dielectric properties of air insulation under the prevailing meteorological conditions of reduced air density (6: 0,8 - 0,85). To facilitate the requisite statistical studies the laboratory is equipped with a microcomputer-based data acquisition system for electrical and meteorological data. The instrumentation and computer equipment are described in detail, as are earthing and screening precautions in the laboratory, Current and future research activities are briefly reviewed and some preliminary results are shown.
